The extremal coefficients $c_p(k)$, complex numbers indexed by $k \in \mathbb{Z}^2$, are as follows. If $p$ is a finite parameter $\mu$, then $c_p(0) = 0$ and $c_p(k) = 2\pi / (|k|^2 (1 + \mu |k|^2))$ for $k \neq 0$. nodes.summary: An extremal parameter is either a finite extremal parameter, that is, a real number $\mu$ with $\mu < -1$ or $\mu > 0$, or one of two further parameters: the first-shell parameter, standing for the endpoint $\mu = -1$, and the biharmonic parameter, standing for the endpoint $\mu = \infty$.

nodes.summary: A finite extremal parameter is a real number $\mu$ with $\mu < -1$ or $\mu > 0$.

nodes.summary:
Write $|k|^2 = k_1^2 + k_2^2$ for a frequency $k \in \mathbb{Z}^2$. A finite extremal parameter $\mu$ is kernel-admissible when $|k|^2 
eq 0$ and $1 + \mu |k|^2 
eq 0$ for every nonzero frequency $k$; the first-shell parameter is always kernel-admissible; the biharmonic parameter is kernel-admissible when $|k|^2 
eq 0$ for every nonzero frequency $k$.
nodes.title: Kernel-admissible extremal parameters

nodes.summary: Two continuous real functions $u$ and $v$ on the torus $\mathbb{T} = (\mathbb{R}/2\pi\mathbb{Z})^2$ lie in the same extremal orbit when there are a real number $a \neq 0$ and a point $x_0 \in \mathbb{T}$ such that $v(x) = a \, u(x - x_0)$ for every $x \in \mathbb{T}$.
